expectedText:
FEHA HOUSING DISCRIMINATION — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for 123 Main St., Los Angeles, CA · Jane Doe

PURPOSE OF THIS INFORMATION SHEET
This information sheet describes the housing-discrimination provisions of California's Fair Employment and Housing Act (Government Code section 12955 et seq.) as they may apply to the property at 123 Main St., Los Angeles, CA. It states what California law provides regarding discrimination in the sale, rental, lease, and financing of housing accommodations in this state -- the statute's own definitions of "housing accommodation" and "owner," the characteristics it protects, examples of what the statute treats as discrimination, and a separate, specifically cross-referenced anti-discrimination statute (the Unruh Civil Rights Act). It does not authorize, direct, or prohibit any particular transaction or practice at 123 Main St., Los Angeles, CA or elsewhere, and it does not tell any reader what to do about a specific property, application, or dispute.

SCOPE: "HOUSING ACCOMMODATION," "OWNER," AND REAL ESTATE-RELATED TRANSACTIONS
The statute defines "housing accommodation" broadly: any building, structure, or portion of one that is occupied, or intended for occupancy, as a residence by one or more families, and any vacant land offered for sale or lease for the construction of such a building or structure -- a definition that separately extends to a dwelling occupied, or intended to be occupied, through a transaction facilitated by a short-term-rental hosting platform. The statute's definition of "owner" is likewise broad: it includes not only a title holder but a lessee, sublessee, assignee, managing agent, real estate broker or salesperson, or any other person holding a legal or equitable right of ownership or possession or the right to rent or lease a housing accommodation, as well as the state and its political subdivisions and agencies. A separate definition reaches the financing side of housing: "real estate-related transactions" include the making or purchasing of loans or providing other financial assistance for purchasing, constructing, improving, repairing, or maintaining a dwelling, or secured by residential real estate.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "“Housing accommodation” means any building, structure, or portion thereof that is occupied as, or intended for occupancy as, a residence by one or more families and any vacant land that is offered for sale or lease for the construction thereon of any building, structure, or portion thereof intended to be so occupied."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12927(d) (California Legislative Information text), Government Code, definition of "housing accommodation" (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12927.)
  "“Owner” includes the lessee, sublessee, assignee, managing agent, real estate broker or salesperson, or any person having any legal or equitable right of ownership or possession or the right to rent or lease housing accommodations, and includes the state and any of its political subdivisions and any agency thereof."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12927(e) (California Legislative Information text), Government Code, definition of "owner" (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12927.)
  "“Real estate-related transactions” include any of the following: (1) The making or purchasing of loans or providing other financial assistance that is for the purpose of purchasing, constructing, improving, repairing, or maintaining a dwelling, or that is secured by residential real estate."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12927(h)(1) (California Legislative Information text), Government Code, definition of "real estate-related transactions" (financing) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12927.)
  Known gap: These three definitions -- "housing accommodation," "owner," and "real estate-related transactions" -- are subdivisions (d), (e), and (h) of the same statutory section, Government Code section 12927, not independent sources of each other; each is quoted below from that one section. Section 12927 states that its definitions apply "as used in this part in connection with housing accommodations," and the prohibited-practices section quoted elsewhere in this document, Government Code section 12955, sits within that same part (Part 2.8 of Division 3 of Title 2) -- this document treats section 12927's definitions as governing section 12955's terms on that textual basis, but did not separately verify every intervening section of the part. The "real estate-related transactions" definition has two further categories this clause does not quote: the selling, brokering, or appraising of residential real property, and certain territorial-underwriting requirements tied to earthquake insurance -- summarized here but not independently verified against the statute's exact wording. Section 12927(c)(2) also states that "discrimination" does not include an owner's refusal to rent or lease a portion of an owner-occupied single-family house to a roomer or boarder living within the household, under stated conditions -- an exception to the general scope this document does not quote or further verify.

PROTECTED CHARACTERISTICS UNDER FEHA'S HOUSING-DISCRIMINATION ARTICLE
Government Code section 12955(a) makes it unlawful for the owner of any housing accommodation to discriminate against or harass any person because of that person's race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information. A separate subdivision of the same section states that this list of characteristics, wherever it is used in the section, includes a perception that a person has any of those characteristics, or that the person is associated with someone who has, or is perceived to have, any of those characteristics.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "(a) For the owner of any housing accommodation to discriminate against or harass any person because of the race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information of that person."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12955(a) (California Legislative Information text), Government Code, housing-discrimination protected characteristics (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12955.)
  "(m) As used in this section, “race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information,” includes a perception that the person has any of those characteristics or that the person is associated with a person who has, or is perceived to have, any of those characteristics."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12955(m) (California Legislative Information text), Government Code, perceived or associational discrimination (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12955.)
  Known gap: Government Code section 12955(a) and section 12955(m) are two subdivisions of the same statutory section, not independent sources of each other. This document verifies the housing-discrimination protected-characteristics list stated in section 12955 itself; it does not independently verify Government Code section 12940, FEHA's separate employment-discrimination section, or confirm point-by-point how that list compares to this one -- 12940 was not fetched as part of this research, so this document does not assert any specific similarity or difference between the two lists beyond what each states on its own. Several of the listed terms ("disability," "familial status," "source of income," "genetic information") are themselves given further statutory definitions elsewhere in this part (for example, section 12955.3 defines "disability" and section 12927 defines "source of income") that are not restated in this clause; "source of income" is addressed in a separate clause of this document.

EXAMPLES OF PROHIBITED PRACTICES: REFUSAL, TERMS, AND ADVERTISING
The statute's definitional section states that "discrimination," for purposes of the housing-discrimination provisions, includes a list of specific practices: refusal to sell, rent, or lease housing accommodations; refusal to negotiate for their sale, rental, or lease; representing that a housing accommodation is not available for inspection, sale, or rental when it is in fact available; any other denial or withholding of housing accommodations; providing inferior terms, conditions, privileges, facilities, or services in connection with housing accommodations; harassment in connection with housing accommodations; cancellation or termination of a sale or rental agreement; and providing segregated or separated housing accommodations. Separately, the prohibited-practices section itself makes it unlawful for any person to make, print, or publish, or cause to be made, printed, or published, any notice, statement, or advertisement regarding the sale or rental of a housing accommodation that indicates a preference, limitation, or discrimination based on the characteristics that section protects, or an intention to make such a preference, limitation, or discrimination.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "(c) (1) “Discrimination” includes refusal to sell, rent, or lease housing accommodations; includes refusal to negotiate for the sale, rental, or lease of housing accommodations; includes representation that a housing accommodation is not available for inspection, sale, or rental when that housing accommodation is in fact so available; includes any other denial or withholding of housing accommodations; includes provision of inferior terms, conditions, privileges, facilities, or services in connection with those housing accommodations; includes harassment in connection with those housing accommodations; includes the cancellation or termination of a sale or rental agreement; includes the provision of segregated or separated housing accommodations"
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12927(c)(1) (California Legislative Information text), Government Code, definition of "discrimination" for housing-accommodation purposes (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12927.)
  "(c) For any person to make, print, or publish, or cause to be made, printed, or published any notice, statement, or advertisement, with respect to the sale or rental of a housing accommodation that indicates any preference, limitation, or discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information or an intention to make"
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12955(c) (California Legislative Information text), Government Code, prohibition on discriminatory advertising (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12955.)
  Known gap: The discrimination-definition quote is drawn from Government Code section 12927(c)(1); the advertising prohibition is drawn from a separate section, Government Code section 12955(c) -- these are independent statutory sections, not subdivisions of the same one, though section 12927 states its definitions govern terms as used in the same part that contains section 12955. Section 12927(c)(1) contains further listed practices this clause does not quote, including refusal to permit a disabled person to make reasonable modifications to premises at the disabled person's expense (subject to a landlord's right, in a rental, to condition permission on restoring the interior afterward) and refusal to make reasonable accommodations in rules, policies, practices, or services necessary for a disabled person's equal use and enjoyment of a dwelling; this document does not restate those disability-specific provisions in full. Section 12955 itself lists further prohibited practices beyond advertising that this clause does not cover, including retaliation against a person who has opposed a practice the section makes unlawful (subdivision (f)), aiding, abetting, inciting, compelling, or coercing any of the acts the section declares unlawful (subdivision (g)), blockbusting -- inducing a sale or rental through representations about the entry of persons of a particular protected characteristic into the neighborhood (subdivision (h)) -- discrimination in real estate-related transactions and appraisals (subdivision (i)), denial of access to a multiple listing service or similar real estate service (subdivision (j)), and discrimination through public or private land use practices, decisions, and authorizations, including restrictive covenants and certain zoning and permit denials (subdivision (l)).

"SOURCE OF INCOME" AS A PROTECTED CHARACTERISTIC
"Source of income" is one of the characteristics section 12955(a) protects. The statute defines it, for purposes of that section, as lawful, verifiable income paid directly to a tenant, to a representative of a tenant, or to a housing owner or landlord on behalf of a tenant -- including federal, state, or local public assistance and federal, state, or local housing subsidies, such as (but not limited to) federal housing assistance vouchers issued under Section 8 of the United States Housing Act of 1937. The definition separately states that "source of income" includes a federal Department of Housing and Urban Development Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing voucher, and that for purposes of this definition a housing owner or landlord is not treated as a tenant's "representative" unless the source of income is that specific type of voucher.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "(p) (1) For the purposes of this section, “source of income” means lawful, verifiable income paid directly to a tenant, or to a representative of a tenant, or paid to a housing owner or landlord on behalf of a tenant, including federal, state, or local public assistance, and federal, state, or local housing subsidies, including, but not limited to, federal housing assistance vouchers issued under Section 8 of the United States Housing Act of 1937 (42 U.S.C. Sec. 1437f). “Source of income” includes a federal Department of Housing and Urban Development Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing voucher. For the purposes of this section, a housing owner or landlord is not considered a representative of a tenant unless the source of income is a federal Department of Housing and Urban Development Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing voucher."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12955(p)(1) (California Legislative Information text), Government Code, definition of "source of income" (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12955.)
  Known gap: This clause quotes Government Code section 12955(p)(1); a materially identical definition of "source of income" also appears in the separate definitional section, Government Code section 12927(i) -- this document treats the two as duplicative restatements within the same part rather than independent corroboration, and did not attempt to verify whether their wording is word-for-word identical. A separate subdivision, section 12955(p)(2) (not quoted here), states that it does not constitute source-of-income discrimination to make a written or oral inquiry about the level or source of a person's income. This clause does not cover the additional source-of-income protections in section 12955(o), which govern income-standard and credit-history practices specifically where a government rent subsidy is involved.

RELATIONSHIP TO THE UNRUH CIVIL RIGHTS ACT (CIVIL CODE § 51)
FEHA's housing-discrimination section itself cross-references a separate California civil rights statute: it makes it unlawful for any person subject to Civil Code section 51 -- as that section applies to housing accommodations -- to discriminate against any person on the basis of a list of characteristics substantially overlapping the one section 12955(a) protects, or on any other basis Civil Code section 51 prohibits. Civil Code section 51, cited by that cross-reference, is the Unruh Civil Rights Act. Unruh states that all persons within California's jurisdiction, regardless of sex, race, color, religion, ancestry, national origin, disability, medical condition, genetic information, marital status, sexual orientation, citizenship, primary language, or immigration status, are entitled to full and equal accommodations, advantages, facilities, privileges, or services in all business establishments of every kind whatsoever.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "(d) For any person subject to the provisions of Section 51 of the Civil Code, as that section applies to housing accommodations, to discriminate against any person on the basis of sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, color, race, religion, ancestry, national origin, familial status, marital status, disability, genetic information, source of income, veteran or military status, or on any other basis prohibited by that section."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12955(d) (California Legislative Information text), Government Code, cross-reference to the Unruh Civil Rights Act as applied to housing (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12955.)
  "(a) This section shall be known, and may be cited, as the Unruh Civil Rights Act."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 51(a) (California Legislative Information text), Civil Code, short title of the Unruh Civil Rights Act (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=51.)
  "(b) All persons within the jurisdiction of this state are free and equal, and no matter what their sex, race, color, religion, ancestry, national origin, disability, medical condition, genetic information, marital status, sexual orientation, citizenship, primary language, or immigration status are entitled to the full and equal accommodations, advantages, facilities, privileges, or services in all business establishments of every kind whatsoever."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 51(b) (California Legislative Information text), Civil Code, Unruh Civil Rights Act general nondiscrimination rule (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=51.)
  Known gap: This clause draws on two independently enacted statutes: Government Code section 12955(d), which is the FEHA housing-discrimination provision's own cross-reference to Civil Code section 51, and Civil Code section 51 itself (the Unruh Civil Rights Act), fetched and verified separately. Section 12955(d)'s cross-reference is the verified basis for stating that Unruh applies to housing accommodations in some respect -- the words "as that section applies to housing accommodations" appear in the FEHA text itself, quoted below. Unruh's own text, by contrast, speaks generally of "business establishments of every kind whatsoever" and does not itself use the word "housing" in the portion quoted here; this document does not independently verify, from statutory text alone, every respect in which -- or every type of housing transaction to which -- Unruh has been held to apply, since that is developed through case law this research did not review. The two statutes' protected-characteristic lists are not identical: Unruh's list quoted here includes citizenship, primary language, immigration status, and medical condition, none of which appear in the FEHA housing list quoted in this document's protected-characteristics clause, while the FEHA housing list includes source of income, familial status, and veteran or military status, none of which appear in the portion of Unruh quoted here. This document does not resolve which statute, if either, would govern a specific situation, or whether both could apply to the same facts.

ACKNOWLEDGMENT
This information sheet regarding the housing-discrimination provisions of California's Fair Employment and Housing Act (Government Code section 12955 et seq.), concerning the property at 123 Main St., Los Angeles, CA, states California law as of the date below. It does not constitute legal advice about, and does not resolve, any specific housing transaction, application, or dispute.

Prepared by: Jane Doe

Date: January 1, 2026

City, state: Los Angeles, California

expectedJSON.gap: This clause draws on two independently enacted statutes: Government Code section 12955(d), which is the FEHA housing-discrimination provision's own cross-reference to Civil Code section 51, and Civil Code section 51 itself (the Unruh Civil Rights Act), fetched and verified separately. Section 12955(d)'s cross-reference is the verified basis for stating that Unruh applies to housing accommodations in some respect -- the words "as that section applies to housing accommodations" appear in the FEHA text itself, quoted below. Unruh's own text, by contrast, speaks generally of "business establishments of every kind whatsoever" and does not itself use the word "housing" in the portion quoted here; this document does not independently verify, from statutory text alone, every respect in which -- or every type of housing transaction to which -- Unruh has been held to apply, since that is developed through case law this research did not review. The two statutes' protected-characteristic lists are not identical: Unruh's list quoted here includes citizenship, primary language, immigration status, and medical condition, none of which appear in the FEHA housing list quoted in this document's protected-characteristics clause, while the FEHA housing list includes source of income, familial status, and veteran or military status, none of which appear in the portion of Unruh quoted here. This document does not resolve which statute, if either, would govern a specific situation, or whether both could apply to the same facts.
